task_description: You're defining a tool with the AI SDK. In v4 you used 'parameters' for the Zod schema. Migrate this tool definition to v5.
deprecated_pattern: tool({ description: 'Get weather', parameters: z.object({ city: z.string() }), execute: async ({ city }) => city })
correct_pattern: tool({ description: 'Get weather', inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string() }), execute: async ({ city }) => city })
why_models_fail_this: Models trained on v4 docs consistently emit 'parameters' because that was the only valid key for tool input schema for years. The rename to 'inputSchema' in v5 is non-obvious from context alone.

task_description: You're calling generateText with a token limit. In v4 the option was named 'maxTokens'. Update this call for v5.
why_models_fail_this: maxTokens is the most common name for this parameter across virtually every LLM SDK. Models confidently produce 'maxTokens' regardless of which SDK version is in scope.

task_description: Your v4 code imports CoreMessage from 'ai'. This type was renamed in v5. Fix the import.
why_models_fail_this: CoreMessage was the canonical message type export from 'ai' throughout v3 and v4. Every v4 tutorial, example and StackOverflow answer uses this name. Models produce it reflexively.

task_description: You're converting UI messages to model messages before calling streamText. The v4 helper was convertToCoreMessages. Update to v5.
deprecated_pattern:
import { convertToCoreMessages } from 'ai';
const messages = convertToCoreMessages(uiMessages);
correct_pattern:
import { convertToModelMessages } from 'ai';
const messages = convertToModelMessages(uiMessages);
why_models_fail_this: convertToCoreMessages was the standard message conversion utility documented in all v4 Next.js examples. The rename to convertToModelMessages mirrors the CoreMessage->ModelMessage type rename but models don't automatically infer this.

task_description: Your v4 route uses StreamData to attach custom metadata to a streaming response. StreamData was removed in v5. Rewrite this using the v5 approach.
why_models_fail_this: StreamData was the only mechanism for custom streaming data in v3 and v4 and appeared in countless tutorials. The replacement is a completely different API surface that models have no training signal for.

task_description: Your React component imports useChat from 'ai/react'. This sub-path was removed in v5. Fix the import.
why_models_fail_this: The 'ai/react' subpath export was used in every v4 React integration example. The move to a separate @ai-sdk/react package requires knowing about the package split, which happened between v4 and v5.

task_description: Your Next.js App Router code imports createStreamableValue from 'ai/rsc'. That sub-path no longer exists in v5. Update it.
why_models_fail_this: ai/rsc was the canonical import for RSC streaming helpers throughout the entire v3/v4 era and was prominent in the Vercel AI SDK documentation. Models always produce this path for RSC utilities.

task_description: You're passing provider-specific options to generateText using 'providerMetadata' as the input parameter key. This key was renamed in v5. Fix it.
deprecated_pattern: generateText({ model, prompt: 'Hello', providerMetadata: { openai: { store: false } } })
correct_pattern: generateText({ model, prompt: 'Hello', providerOptions: { openai: { store: false } } })
why_models_fail_this: providerMetadata was used for both input and output in v4. In v5 only the input was renamed to providerOptions while the output property kept its name. Models conflate the two and use the old name for inputs.

task_description: You're iterating over fullStream to inspect tool call arguments. In v4 the property was called 'args'. Update the stream handler to v5.
why_models_fail_this: part.args was used in every v4 streaming example for tool call inspection. The simultaneous rename of both args->input and result->output for tool stream parts is easy to miss, and models default to the old names.

task_description: You have a multi-step agent using generateText with maxSteps to limit iterations. This option was removed in v5. Rewrite it using the v5 API.
correct_pattern:
import { stepCountIs } from 'ai';
generateText({ model, messages, stopWhen: stepCountIs(5), tools })
why_models_fail_this: maxSteps was the universally used option for agentic loops in v4. The replacement is an entirely new composable stopWhen API with helper functions from a named export, which models have no prior training signal for.

task_description: You're reading the reasoning text from a generateText result in a multi-step call using step.reasoning. This property was renamed in v5. Fix the accessor.
why_models_fail_this: step.reasoning was the property in v4 for reading reasoning/thinking output. The v5 rename to reasoningText for the string form (while repurposing reasoning as the detail array) is an asymmetric change that models will get wrong.

task_description: You're reading message text from a useChat message using message.content. In v5 the Message type was replaced with UIMessage and the content field was replaced with a parts array. Update your render code.
why_models_fail_this: message.content as a plain string was used in every single useChat UI example for years. The shift to a parts array is a fundamental structural change that requires understanding the new UIMessage type, which pre-v5 models have no knowledge of.

task_description: You're sending an image message to a model using mimeType. This property was renamed in v5. Fix the message content object.
why_models_fail_this: mimeType is the standard term used across browser APIs, HTTP headers, and older LLM SDKs. The rename to mediaType is an internal convention change that models won't infer.

task_description: Your generateText call uses experimental_continueSteps to work around output token limits. This option was removed in v5. How do you handle long outputs now?
why_models_fail_this: experimental_continueSteps was a known workaround for token limits documented in AI SDK v3/v4. Models will confidently include it when asked to generate long text. The removal with no direct replacement is a hard change to guess.

task_description: You're accessing tool results from a stream part using part.result. In v5 this property was renamed. Fix the property access.
why_models_fail_this: part.result was used in all v4 streaming examples alongside part.args. The simultaneous rename of args->input and result->output affects both sides of tool call/result and models trained on v4 produce the old names.

task_description: In your v4 UI code you check for message parts with type 'tool-invocation'. In v5 the part type scheme changed to use the tool name. Update the part type check for a tool called 'getWeather'.
why_models_fail_this: The 'tool-invocation' generic part type was the only mechanism for tool UI parts in v4 and appeared in every useChat + tools example. The shift to per-tool typed part names is a fundamental type system redesign that models trained on v4 cannot anticipate.

task_description: Your v4 UI checks toolInvocation.state === 'result' to know if a tool has finished. In v5 the state values were renamed. Update the state check.
why_models_fail_this: The v4 states (partial-call, call, result) were documented in every AI SDK + tools tutorial. The complete rename to input-streaming/input-available/output-available/output-error is a non-obvious four-way change. Models confidently produce the old state names.

task_description: You're using dataStream.writeData() and dataStream.writeMessageAnnotation() in a createDataStreamResponse handler. Both methods were removed in v5. Migrate to the new approach.
correct_pattern: createUIMessageStream({ execute({ writer }) { writer.write({ type: 'data-event', id: 'e1', data: 'started' }); writer.write({ type: 'data-annotation', id: 'a1', data: { id: '1' } }); } })
why_models_fail_this: writeData and writeMessageAnnotation were documented alongside createDataStreamResponse in every v4 custom streaming guide. The entire data streaming API was replaced in v5 and the old methods no longer exist.
